chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said:
The hand of the thief is cut, and his thumb is left, along with the center of his palm; and his leg is cut, and his heel is left for him so he may walk upon it.
ai.seo_question: What are the precise anatomical details of cutting the hand and leg for the theft penalty in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the precise anatomical boundaries for the hadd penalty of theft, emphasizing the preservation of the thumb and heel to ensure the offender retains mobility and functionality for repentance and reintegration. It reflects the Shia juristic principle of balancing strict legal retribution with mercy, ensuring the punishment is severe yet minimally disabling. The detailed description underscores the importance of procedural exactitude in applying divine law as transmitted through the Imams.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said:
‘The hand of the thief would be cut and his thumb would be left alone along with the centre of the palm; and his leg would be cut and his sole would be left alone so he can walk upon it’.
